56.reason: An electrical impulse always travels through a neuron in one fixed direction: dendrite -> cell body -> axon -> axon terminal, and then across the synapse to the dendrite of the next neuron. Only option B shows this sequence — dendrites/cell body on the left, axon extending right to the terminal, arrows pointing rightward, and the first neuron’s terminal feeding the second neuron’s dendrites. Option C has the same correct layout but arrows reversed (backward), option A runs the chain in the wrong overall direction, and option D mirrors the second neuron so two axon terminals face each other (an impossible terminal-to-terminal synapse). Hence B.
